You need to ensure that you can manage the domain password policies from Server1.

questions.explanation:

questions.explanation:
The Central Store takes precedence over local ADMX policy-definition files when Group Policy Administrative Templates are edited. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have three on-premises Windows Server computers named SVR1, SVR2, and SVR3. SRV1 contains a direct-attached storage (DAS) array.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a server named Server1 that hosts Windows containers.  
  
You plan to deploy an application consisting of multiple containers. Each container will reside on the same subnet. Each container requires its own MAC address and IP address, and must be able to communicate by using its IP address.  
  
You need to create a Docker network that supports deployment of the application.  
  
Which type of network should you create?
questions.explanation:
A transparent network connects container endpoints directly to the physical network through an external Hyper-V switch. Each container can receive its own physical-network IP address and retains a distinct MAC address, enabling direct communication by IP address. In contrast, L2bridge rewrites container MAC addresses to the host MAC address.

**Learn more:** [Windows container network drivers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/container-networking/network-drivers-topologies)

DNS Manager can configure a DNS zone to use a partition, but it does not create the required Active Directory application partition with the selected replica scope.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1 that has only a private IP address.  
  
You configure the Windows Admin Center extension on VM1.  
  
You have an on-premises computer running Windows 11, which you use for server management.  
  
You need to ensure that Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal can be used to manage VM1.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: an Azure Bastion host on the virtual network that contains VM1.
a VPN connection to the virtual network that contains VM1.
a private endpoint on the virtual network that contains VM1.
a network security group (NSG) rule that allows inbound traffic on port 443.

questions.explanation:
Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal requires inbound connectivity to a direct IP address of the VM on the port where Windows Admin Center is installed. For a VM that has only a private IP address, a VPN connection to the virtual network provides the required private-network connectivity. Microsoft documents that Azure Bastion is not supported for Windows Admin Center in the Azure portal, and the documented Windows Admin Center inbound port is 6516 by default, not 443.

**Learn more:** [Manage a Windows VM using Windows Admin Center in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/manage/windows-admin-center/azure/manage-vm)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named contoso.com. The domain includes two Windows Server servers named Server1 and Server2. The domain also includes two users named User1 and User2.  
  
You perform these tasks:  
  
- Enable Remote SSH Access on Server2.  
- Sign in to Server1 as User1.  
  
You need to establish an SSH session from Server1 to Server2 and sign in as User2.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
The Windows OpenSSH client uses the `ssh domain\username@servername` syntax to connect to a remote SSH server as a specified domain user. Therefore, `ssh Contoso\User2@Server2` connects to Server2 as Contoso\User2. `sshd` is the server daemon, not the client connection command.

**Learn more:** [Get started with OpenSSH Server for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh_install_firstuse)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. The domain includes 10 servers running Windows Server, each with a static IP address.  
  
You plan to use DHCP to assign IP addresses to the servers. You must ensure that every server always receives the same IP address.  
  
Which type of identifier should you use to create a DHCP reservation for each server?
questions.explanation:
A DHCP reservation binds a specific IP address to a DHCP client identifier. For Windows DHCP clients, the client identifier is the NIC’s MAC address, so the server receives the same reserved address whenever it requests a lease.

**Learn more:** [Install and configure DHCP Server on Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/dhcp/quickstart-install-configure-dhcp-server) · [Add-DhcpServerv4Reservation (DhcpServer)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/dhcpserver/add-dhcpserverv4reservation?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

What should you do?

Modify the priority of Rule1 and add an inbound port rule.

Installing the Windows Admin Center Azure extension requires outbound TCP 443 connectivity from the VM to the `WindowsAdminCenter` service tag. Changing that rule's priority allows a specific outbound allow rule for the Windows Admin Center service to be evaluated first. [Manage a Windows VM using Windows Admin Center in Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/manage/windows-admin-center/azure/manage-vm)

To which subnets can NIC1 be attached?
questions.explanation:

questions.explanation:
Cluster Shared Volumes (CSV) allow multiple nodes in a Windows Server failover cluster to simultaneously read from and write to the same shared LUN, presenting it as a single consistent file namespace (typically under C:\ClusterStorage). This is the storage configuration required for highly available Hyper-V virtual machines because it enables live migration—VMs can move between nodes without needing to dismount/remount the disk resource, since all nodes maintain concurrent access to the volume. User1 and both security groups synchronize to Entra ID through Azure AD Connect regardless of group scope — Azure AD Connect syncs universal and domain-local security groups alike — so no scope change is required. Changing Group2 to Universal (D) is unnecessary because domain-local groups already sync and work in CA.

You have an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain that contains three Windows Server computers named Server1, Server2, and Server3.  
  
You sign in to Server1 with a domain account and initiate a remote PowerShell session to Server2. From that remote PowerShell session, you try to access a resource on Server3, but access to the resource is denied.  
  
You need to ensure that your credentials are delegated from Server1 to Server3. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy a DHCP availability solution that fulfills the networking requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: On DHCP1, create a scope that contains 25 percent of the IP addresses from Scope2.
On the router in each office, configure a DHCP relay.
DHCP2, configure a scope that contains 25 percent of the IP addresses from Scope1.
On each DHCP server, install the Failover Clustering feature and add the DHCP cluster role.
On each DHCP scope, configure DHCP failover.

questions.explanation:
DHCP failover synchronizes IPv4 scope configuration and active leases between two DHCP servers, allowing either failover partner to continue leasing addresses when the other is unavailable. DHCP requests begin as subnet broadcasts, which routers do not ordinarily forward; DHCP relay on each office router forwards those requests to the DHCP servers. DHCP failover does not use Failover Clustering or a 25-percent split-scope configuration.

**Learn more:** [DHCP failover in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/dhcp/dhcp-failover) · [Install DHCP relay agent for Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/dhcp/dhcp-deploy-relay-agent)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises server named Server1 that runs Windows Server. Server1 hosts an app named App1 and a firewall named Firewall1.  
  
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
Internal users access App1 by using WebSockets.  
  
You need to make App1 accessible to users on the internet. The solution must minimize the number of inbound ports opened on Firewall1.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Relay Hybrid Connections supports HTTP and WebSockets and securely exposes an on-premises endpoint through an outbound connection from the on-premises listener to Azure Relay. Because internet clients connect to the Relay rather than directly to Server1, Firewall1 does not need inbound ports opened for App1.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes a multi-site Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest. Each Active Directory site is connected by manually configured site links and automatically generated connections.  
  
You need to reduce the convergence time for Active Directory changes.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: For each site link, modify the replication schedule.
For each site links, modify the site link costs.
Create a site link bridge that contains all the site links.
For each site link, modify the options attribute.

questions.explanation:
Enable change notification on every site link by modifying its `options` attribute. Change notification prompts intersite replication when directory changes occur, rather than waiting for the normal scheduled replication interval, thereby reducing Active Directory convergence time.

**Learn more:** [Set-ADReplicationSiteLink (ActiveDirectory)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/set-adreplicationsitelink?view=windowsserver2025-ps) · [Introduction to Active Directory Replication and Topology Management Using Windows PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/powershell/introduction-to-active-directory-replication-and-topology-management-using-windows-powershell--level-100-)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest named contoso.com. The forest root domain has a server named server1.contoso.com.  
  
A two-way forest trust is configured between the contoso.com forest and an AD DS forest named fabrikam.com. The fabrikam.com forest has 10 child domains.  
  
You must ensure that only members of a group named fabrikam\Group1 can authenticate to server1.contoso.com.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add fabrikam\Group1 to the local Users group on server1.contoso.com.
Enable SID filtering for the trust.
Enable Selective authentication for the trust.
Change the trust to a one-way external trust.

questions.explanation:
Selective authentication on a forest trust requires users from the other forest to be explicitly authorized to authenticate to each local resource. After enabling it, grant fabrikam\Group1 the Allowed to Authenticate permission on server1.contoso.com; this prevents other fabrikam.com users from authenticating to that server.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine with these configurations:  
  
- Name: VM1  
- Size: Standard DS1 v2  
- Operating system: Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition  
  
VM1 has an OS disk named Disk0 with these configurations:  
  
- Size: 127 GB  
- Type: Standard SSD  
- Redundancy: Locally-redundant storage (LRS)  
  
You perform these actions:  
  
- In the Azure portal, you add a new data disk named Disk1 to VM1.  
- On VM1, you install an app named App1.  
  
You need to ensure that Disk1 is used as the D drive on VM1. The solution must ensure that data written by App1 to drive D is retained when VM1 restarts.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Move Pagefile.sys to the C drive.
From Disk Management, change the drive letter assigned to the volume on Disk0.
From Disk Management, change the drive letter assigned to the volume on Disk1.
Resize VM1 to Standard DS2 v2.

questions.explanation:
On Azure Windows VMs, D: is the temporary disk by default and commonly hosts `Pagefile.sys`. To make a persistent data disk use D:, temporarily move `Pagefile.sys` to C: before changing the temporary disk’s drive letter and assigning D: to the data disk. This prevents App1 data from being stored on temporary storage.

**Learn more:** [Use the D: drive as a data drive on a Windows VM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/change-drive-letter)

You have a Hyper-V host.  
  
You are assessing the available schedulers.  
  
Which scheduler type provides the greatest isolation between guests and the host?
questions.explanation:
The core scheduler assigns a VM’s virtual processors to sibling logical processors of the same physical core and does not share that core with other VMs. This creates a strong guest-workload isolation boundary and mitigates side-channel exposure across partitions, including the root partition.\

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783863285329-xtgqcy43.png)  
  
To which DNS servers is Zone1.com replicated?
questions.explanation:
Zone1.com is Active Directory-Integrated with the replication scope set to "All DNS servers in this domain." An AD-integrated zone is stored in the DomainDnsZones application directory partition and is replicated by Active Directory replication, which only reaches DNS servers that are also domain controllers in that domain (contoso.com). Server2 is a DC + DNS server in contoso.com, so it receives a copy. Server3 is a DNS server but NOT a domain controller, so it cannot hold the AD-integrated copy; Server4 and Server5 belong to east.contoso.com and are outside "this domain." Since the zone was created on Server1, the only additional server it replicates to is Server2.

**Learn more:** [AD-Integrated DNS Zones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/active-directory-integrated-dns-zones) · [Integrating AD DS with DNS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/integrating-ad-ds-into-an-existing-dns-infrastructure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has a multi-site Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) forest. Each Active Directory site is connected by manually configured site links and automatically generated connections.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must satisfy the technical requirements for VM2.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable the Guest services integration service.

questions.explanation:
The technical requirement for VM2 is to force users to provide credentials when they connect through Virtual Machine Connection (VMConnect) so that an administrator cannot inherit another administrator's already signed-in console session. Enhanced session mode changes VMConnect from a raw console attach to a Remote Desktop (RDP) style connection to the guest, which requires the connecting user to authenticate to the guest OS and treats each connection as a new interactive logon. Guest service integration only enables host-to-guest file copy, Credential Guard protects LSASS secrets inside Windows (it doesn't govern VMConnect logon behavior), and shielded VMs provide fabric-level protection - none of these force per-connection credentials. Therefore you enable enhanced session mode.

**Learn more:** [Use local resources on Hyper-V with VMConnect (enhanced session mode)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/learn-more/use-local-resources-on-hyper-v-virtual-machine-with-vmconnect)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a server named Server1 running Windows Server 2019 that hosts a container named Container1. Container1 uses a Windows Server 2019 base image built by using a Docker file.  
  
You upgrade Server1 to Windows Server 2022.  
  
You need to ensure that Container1 runs on Server1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Start Container1 in Hyper-V isolation mode.
Start Container1 in process isolation mode.

Server1 hosts the parent `contoso.local` zone and contains delegations for both child zones, so it can direct queries to the authoritative DNS servers for `east.contoso.local` and `west.contoso.local`. As the forwarder, Server1 can also resolve Internet names by using its root hints. Microsoft documents that a parent-zone DNS server uses delegation information before forwarding, and that root hints enable recursive resolution.\
\

Solution: On Server2, create conditional forwarders for **contoso.local** and **west.contoso.local**. On Server3, create conditional forwarders for **contoso.local** and **east.contoso.local**.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Conditional forwarders send queries for designated DNS suffixes to the configured DNS servers, with the more specific child-zone forwarder handling child-zone queries. Server1 can resolve the parent zone and refer delegated child-zone queries to Server2 or Server3; the two child servers can also forward directly to each other’s child zone. Root hints provide resolution for Internet hosts.\
\
**Learn more:** [DNS Forwarding in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/dns/forwarding) · [Get-IpamDnsConditionalForwarder](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/ipamserver/get-ipamdnsconditionalforwarder?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure a conditional forwarder for `contoso.local` on Server2 and Server3.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A conditional forwarder routes queries for the specified DNS namespace to its configured DNS server. Forwarding `contoso.local` queries from Server2 and Server3 to Server1 provides resolution for the parent zone and lets Server1 use its delegations to reach the east.contoso.local and west.contoso.local zones. Queries for internet hosts can continue to be resolved through root hints. DNS delegation uses NS records to direct resolution into the delegated child zone.\
\
**Learn more:** [DNS Forwarding in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/dns/forwarding) · [DNS Architecture in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/dns/dns-architecture)

Conditional forwarders send queries for the specified DNS domain to the configured DNS servers. Forwarding only between east.contoso.local and west.contoso.local enables resolution of those two child namespaces, but it does not provide Server2 or Server3 with a way to resolve records in the parent contoso.local zone. Public root hints cannot resolve the private contoso.local namespace, so the configuration does not meet the requirement for all internal namespaces.

**Learn more:** [DNS Forwarding in Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/dns/forwarding) · [Add-DnsServerConditionalForwarderZone (DnsServer)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/dnsserver/add-dnsserverconditionalforwarderzone?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

Does this satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation: DHCP address exclusions merely keep specified IP addresses from being leased by the scope. They do not assign a consistent address to a particular printer. DHCP reservations, associated with each printer’s hardware address, are needed to ensure fixed IP assignments.

questions.explanation: A DHCP relay agent only relays DHCP client requests and server responses across subnet boundaries. It does not reserve a particular address for a printer. Consistent DHCP-assigned addresses require DHCP reservations for the printers.

questions.explanation:
